slides.text:
A function is a named piece of code you write once and run as many times as you want. You already wrote one, `main`. Here you declare your own, give them parameters, and make them give a value back.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
name        what to call it
inputs      what it receives
output      what it gives back
body        what it does

slides.text: A function does nothing until something **calls** it. A call can pass values in, and the function can send one value back to the place that called it. The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
result = name(input)

name(input):
    work with input
    give back an answer

exercises.title: Your first function
exercises.guide: Declare a function that prints a line, then call it twice.

chunks.guide: `func` declares a function: a name, parentheses and a body in braces. The body does not run yet.
`main` is a function too. Call `greet` by its name with parentheses. Each call runs the body again.

exercises.title: Pass a value in
exercises.guide: Make the function greet whoever it receives.

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. A **parameter** is a name with a type, inside the parentheses. The body uses it like a variable.

notes.text: Callers must pass a string here.

chunks.guide: The value you pass in a call is an **argument**. It fills the parameter.

exercises.title: More than one parameter
exercises.guide: Describe a person with a name and an age.

chunks.guide: Separate the parameters with commas. Each one has its own type.
Arguments go in the same order as the parameters.

output.text:
Ana is 30 years old
Luis is 25 years old

exercises.title: Type and call
exercises.guide: Give the first parameter its type, and call the function.

exercises.title: Give a value back
exercises.guide: Write a function that adds two numbers and gives the sum back.

chunks.guide: The type after the parentheses is what the function gives back. `return` sends that value to the caller.

notes.text: Ends the function and hands back the value.

chunks.guide: A call that returns a value can be stored in a variable, like any other value.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `square(n)` gives back 9, but nothing stores it, so the value is thrown away. `n` is still 3.

exercises.title: Parameters that share a type
exercises.guide: Compute the area of a rectangle from its two sides.

chunks.guide: Neighbor parameters of the same type can share it: write the type once, after the last name.
A call can sit inside another call. The result goes straight to `Println`.

exercises.title: Finish the function
exercises.guide: Name the second parameter and send the result back.

exercises.title: Functions calling functions
exercises.guide: Build one function on top of another, with `main` first.

chunks.guide: `main` can call a function written below it. Go reads the whole file before it runs.
A function can call another one. The inner call runs first, and its result goes to the outer one.
The helper the others rely on.

exercises.title: What is it for?
exercises.guide: Read the function, then pick what it is for.
options: Tells whether a is greater than b
Gives back the larger of two numbers
Gives back the difference of two numbers
exercises.explanation: It returns `a` when `a` is bigger, and `b` otherwise. It gives back a number, not a yes or no.
